proposal.hypothesis: The baseline optimises pointwise logloss while both metrics rank strictly within a user's list. Any per-row calibration effort is wasted: only within-list score differences matter. A listwise softmax cross-entropy over each user's list directly optimises the ordering, and puts most gradient on the top of the list, which is exactly what nDCG@5 measures; it also implicitly forms all pairs, aligning with GAUC. Measured list sizes say the grouping matters: user_id lists average 43.5 in train versus 5.58 at evaluation, whereas user_id+date averages 5.77 — nearly identical to evaluation. So I train listwise with user_id+date grouping. Softmax is degenerate on single-label lists, so I normalise targets across positives and skip all-positive/all-negative lists (43% of users), whose ordering is unlearnable anyway.
